examples.en: You have to knead the dough for a long time for the noodles to get chewy.

examples.ko: 이 집은 면발이 가늘어서 국물이 잘 배요.
examples.en: The noodles here are thin, so they soak up the broth well.
The noodles got too soggy, so they don't taste good.
For cold noodles, buckwheat noodles are the best.
I twirl a big bunch of noodles around my chopsticks and eat them.

examples.ko: 우동은 면발이 굵을수록 씹는 맛이 좋아요.
examples.en: The thicker the udon noodles are, the better they are to chew.

explain: 국수, 라면, 우동처럼 면 한 가닥 한 가닥의 식감을 말할 때 써요. '쫄깃하다', '탱탱하다', '불다'와 자주 함께 나와요. 음식 종류를 말할 때는 '면'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you talk about the texture of the individual strands in noodle dishes such as guksu, ramyeon and udon. It often appears with '쫄깃하다' (chewy), '탱탱하다' (springy) and '불다' (get soggy). When you talk about the kind of food, people just say '면'.

examples.ko: 신부가 하얀 면사포를 쓰고 걸어 들어왔어요.
examples.en: The bride walked in wearing a white veil.

examples.ko: 면사포가 길어서 걸을 때 밟을 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The veil was so long that I almost stepped on it while walking.

examples.ko: 언니가 결혼식 때 쓸 면사포를 골라요.
examples.en: My older sister is choosing a veil to wear at her wedding.
The veil fluttered a little in the wind.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때 면사포를 뒤로 넘겼어요.
examples.en: I flipped the veil back when we took the photo.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 엄마의 면사포를 써 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I once tried on my mom's veil.

explain: 결혼식에서 신부가 머리에 쓰는 얇고 긴 천이에요. '쓰다', '벗다', '내리다'와 같이 써요. '베일'은 영어에서 온 말로 같은 물건을 가리켜요.
explain_en: This is the long, thin cloth a bride wears on her head at a wedding. It goes with verbs like '쓰다' (wear), '벗다' (take off) and '내리다' (lower). '베일' is a loanword from English that refers to the same item.

examples.ko: 정원 일을 할 때 면장갑을 껴요.
examples.en: I wear cotton gloves when I do garden work.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 면장갑만 껴도 손이 덜 시려요.
examples.en: In winter, even just cotton gloves make your hands less cold.
I bought cotton gloves to carry the moving boxes.
You can wash cotton gloves in the washing machine.

examples.ko: 아빠가 낡은 면장갑을 끼고 페인트칠을 하세요.
examples.en: Dad is painting with a pair of old cotton gloves on.

examples.ko: 피부가 약해서 자기 전에 면장갑을 끼고 자요.
examples.en: My skin is sensitive, so I sleep in cotton gloves.

explain: 집안일이나 작업할 때 끼는 흰색 같은 얇은 장갑이에요. 장갑은 '끼다'를 써서 '면장갑을 끼다'라고 해요. 가죽장갑, 털장갑처럼 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여서 구분해요.
explain_en: These are thin gloves worn for housework or manual work. Gloves take the verb '끼다', so you say '면장갑을 끼다'. Korean names gloves by material at the front, like 가죽장갑 (leather gloves) and 털장갑 (wool gloves).

examples.ko: 김장할 때 멸치젓을 넣으면 감칠맛이 나요.
examples.en: If you add salted anchovies when making kimchi, it gets a rich savory taste.
This is salted anchovy that my grandmother made herself.
The smell of salted anchovies was strong, so it was hard at first.

examples.ko: 멸치젓은 숙성하는 데 몇 달이 걸려요.
examples.en: Salted anchovies take several months to ferment.

examples.ko: 배추김치에 멸치젓 대신 까나리액젓을 넣는 집도 있어요.
examples.en: Some families put sand lance sauce in cabbage kimchi instead of salted anchovies.
Have you ever dipped grilled pork belly in salted anchovies?

explain: 멸치를 소금에 절여 삭힌 젓갈이에요. 주로 김치 양념에 들어가고, 멸치를 걸러 낸 국물은 '멸치액젓'이라고 해요. 발음할 때 받침 ㅅ이 [ㄷ]으로 나서 [멸치젇]이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is a jeotgal (salted seafood) made by salting and fermenting anchovies. It is mainly used in kimchi seasoning, and the liquid strained from it is called '멸치액젓'. The final ㅅ is pronounced like [ㄷ], so it sounds like [멸치젇].

examples.en: I brought braised anchovies as a side dish for my lunchbox.
If you add nuts to the braised anchovies, they taste even nuttier.
The braised anchovies my mom makes are sweet and salty.
Please eat the braised anchovies before they get hard.
There are some braised anchovies left in the fridge.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁은 밥하고 멸치조림만 있어도 충분해요.
examples.en: For dinner today, just rice and braised anchovies is enough.

explain: 작은 멸치를 간장이나 고추장 양념에 조린 밑반찬이에요. 집에서는 '멸치볶음'이라고도 많이 불러요. 도시락 반찬이나 밑반찬 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is a small side dish of little anchovies cooked down in soy sauce or red pepper paste seasoning. At home, many people also call it '멸치볶음'. It comes up often when people talk about lunchbox or everyday side dishes.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 밥에 명란젓을 올려 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It's delicious to eat salted pollack roe on top of warm rice.

examples.ko: 명란젓은 짭짤해서 조금만 먹어도 밥이 넘어가요.
examples.en: Salted pollack roe is salty, so a little of it goes a long way with rice.
I added sesame oil to the salted pollack roe and mixed it.
I bought a tub of salted pollack roe at the supermarket.
I made a rolled omelet with salted pollack roe.

examples.ko: 명란젓이 매운 것도 있고 안 매운 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Some salted pollack roe is spicy and some isn't.

explain: 명태 알을 소금에 절여 만든 젓갈이에요. 밥반찬으로 많이 먹고, 요즘은 파스타나 계란말이에도 넣어요. 발음은 [명난젇]이에요.
explain_en: This is a jeotgal made by salting pollack roe. It is a popular side dish with rice, and these days it also goes into pasta and rolled omelets. It is pronounced [명난젇].

examples.ko: 인사과 직원이 급여 명세서를 메일로 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: A staff member in HR emailed me my pay statement.
There is a payment I don't recognize on my card statement.

examples.ko: 승급 심사 결과는 다음 달 급여 명세서에 반영돼요.
examples.en: The promotion review result will be reflected in next month's pay statement.
Please check your phone bill statement.
Looking at the statement, a lot was taken out for taxes.
I got an itemized medical bill from the hospital.

explain: 돈이 어디에 얼마 쓰였는지 항목별로 적은 문서예요. 영수증이 '냈다'는 증명이라면, 명세서는 안에 든 내용을 자세히 보여 줘요. '급여 명세서', '카드 명세서'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여서 써요.
explain_en: This is a document that lists, item by item, where money went and how much. A receipt proves you paid, while a 명세서 shows the details inside. Put the type in front, as in '급여 명세서' (pay statement) and '카드 명세서' (card statement).

examples.en: My father took voluntary retirement from his company this year.

examples.ko: 명예퇴직을 신청하면 퇴직금 외에 추가 보상을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you apply for voluntary retirement, you can get extra compensation besides severance pay.

examples.ko: 고민 끝에 명예퇴직을 신청했지만 아직도 앞날이 막막해요.
examples.en: After much thought I applied for voluntary retirement, but my future still feels uncertain.
My senior took voluntary retirement and opened a small cafe.
The company is struggling, so more people are taking voluntary retirement.
I'm also torn about whether to take voluntary retirement or not.

explain: 정년이 되기 전에 회사가 주는 보상을 받고 스스로 나가는 것이에요. 그냥 '퇴직하다', '그만두다'와 달리 보상금이 따라오는 제도라는 점이 달라요. 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 줄여서 '명퇴'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means leaving a company of your own will before retirement age while receiving compensation from the company. Unlike plain '퇴직하다' or '그만두다', it comes with a payout under a company program. It appears in news and talk about work, and is often shortened to '명퇴'.

examples.ko: 명태는 말리면 북어, 얼리면 동태가 돼요.
examples.en: Pollack becomes bugeo when dried and dongtae when frozen.
I bought one pollack at the market.
In winter, we make stew with pollack.
People make myeongnanjeot with pollack roe.
I'm picking out the fish meat to make pollack pancakes.
These days it's hard to find domestic pollack.

explain: 같은 명태라도 상태에 따라 이름이 달라요. 신선한 것은 '생태', 얼린 것은 '동태', 말린 것은 '북어'라고 해요. 그래서 찌개를 시킬 때는 '동태찌개', '북엇국'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: The same fish has different names depending on its state: fresh is '생태', frozen is '동태' and dried is '북어'. That is why dishes are called things like '동태찌개' (frozen pollack stew) and '북엇국' (dried pollack soup).

examples.en: On summer nights I put up a mosquito net and sleep.
The windows of the country house have mosquito netting.
There's a hole in the mosquito net, so mosquitoes get in.

examples.ko: 캠핑할 때 텐트 안에 모기장을 달았어요.
examples.en: When we went camping, I hung a mosquito net inside the tent.

examples.ko: 모기장 덕분에 밤새 한 번도 안 물렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the mosquito net, I didn't get bitten even once all night.

examples.ko: 아이 침대 위에 모기장을 걸어 줬어요.
examples.en: I hung a mosquito net over the child's bed.

explain: 자는 곳을 둘러싸서 모기를 막는 그물이에요. '모기장을 치다', '모기장을 걸다'처럼 말해요. 창문에 붙이는 망은 보통 '방충망'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is a net that surrounds a sleeping area to keep mosquitoes out. You say '모기장을 치다' or '모기장을 걸다'. The screen fixed to a window is usually called '방충망'.

examples.en: In math class, I drew a graph on graph paper.

examples.ko: 모눈종이를 쓰면 선을 똑바로 그리기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you use graph paper, it's easy to draw straight lines.
One square on this graph paper is one centimeter.

examples.ko: 모눈종이 위에 도형을 그리고 넓이를 구했어요.
examples.en: I drew a shape on graph paper and found its area.
In art class, I made a pattern using graph paper.

examples.ko: 선생님이 모눈종이를 한 장씩 나눠 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher handed out one sheet of graph paper to each of us.

explain: 가로세로 줄이 그어져 작은 네모 칸이 있는 종이예요. 수학이나 과학 시간에 그래프를 그릴 때 많이 써요. 영어의 graph paper와 같다고 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: This is paper printed with horizontal and vertical lines that form small squares. It is often used in math or science class for drawing graphs. You can think of it as the same as English 'graph paper'.

examples.en: Steam is rising from the ramyeon.

examples.ko: 갓 쪄 낸 만두에서 김이 모락모락 올라와요.
examples.en: Steam is rising from the freshly steamed dumplings.

examples.ko: 국에서 모락모락 피어오르는 김을 보니 배가 고파져요.
examples.en: Seeing the steam curling up from the soup makes me hungry.

examples.ko: 모락모락 김이 나는 고구마를 호호 불어 먹었어요.
examples.en: I blew on the steaming sweet potato and ate it.

examples.ko: 겨울 아침에 따뜻한 밥에서 모락모락 김이 나요.
examples.en: On winter mornings, steam rises from the warm rice.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 입에서도 입김이 모락모락 나요.
examples.en: On cold days, breath comes out of your mouth in puffs too.

explain: 김이나 연기가 천천히 계속 피어오르는 모양이에요. 따뜻한 음식에 쓰는 경우가 많아서 '김이 모락모락 나다'로 가장 자주 써요. '펄펄'처럼 세게 끓는 느낌과 달리 조용히 올라와요.
explain_en: It describes steam or smoke rising slowly and steadily. It is mostly used for warm food, so '김이 모락모락 나다' is the most common form. Unlike '펄펄', which feels like hard boiling, it rises quietly.

examples.ko: 사막에서는 모래바람 때문에 눈을 뜨기 어려워요.
examples.en: In the desert, it's hard to keep your eyes open because of the blowing sand.
The sandy wind blew hard, so I put on a mask.

examples.ko: 해변에 모래바람이 불어 입에 모래가 들어갔어요.
examples.en: Sand blew across the beach and got into my mouth.
I walked through the blowing sand, so my hair is a mess.

examples.ko: 영화 속 사막에는 늘 모래바람이 불어요.
examples.en: In movies, the desert always has sand blowing.
The camel walks slowly to avoid the blowing sand.

explain: 모래를 날리며 부는 바람이에요. 봄에 한국으로 오는 '황사'와는 달라서, 모래바람은 사막이나 해변, 공사장처럼 눈앞에서 모래가 날리는 장면에 써요. '모래바람이 일다', '모래바람이 불다'로 말해요.
explain_en: This is wind that blows sand around. It differs from '황사' (yellow dust), which comes to Korea in spring; 모래바람 is for scenes where sand is flying right in front of you, such as deserts, beaches or construction sites. You say '모래바람이 일다' or '모래바람이 불다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is a model student at school.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 모범적인 사례로 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: That company was on the news as a model example.

examples.ko: 민수는 약속도 잘 지키고 모범적으로 행동해요.
examples.en: Minsu keeps his promises and behaves in an exemplary way.
I got praised thanks to my exemplary attitude.
Our team leader is a model boss.
This is a neighborhood that sorts its trash in an exemplary way.

explain: '모범적인 학생', '모범적으로 행동하다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸며 줘요. '모범적이다'로도 써서 '그 사람은 모범적이에요'라고 말할 수 있어요. 사람의 행동이나 태도를 칭찬할 때 쓰고, 학생을 가리키는 '모범생'도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It modifies what follows, as in '모범적인 학생' (model student) and '모범적으로 행동하다' (behave in an exemplary way). You can also use it as a predicate: '그 사람은 모범적이에요'. It praises someone's behavior or attitude, and it is useful to learn '모범생' (model student) along with it.

examples.en: I took a deluxe taxi to the airport.

examples.ko: 모범택시는 일반 택시보다 요금이 조금 비싸요.
examples.en: Deluxe taxis cost a bit more than regular taxis.
Deluxe taxis are usually black.
I called a deluxe taxi late at night.
I took my parents to the hospital by deluxe taxi.

examples.ko: 모범택시 기사님이 친절하게 짐을 실어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The deluxe taxi driver kindly loaded my luggage.

explain: 검은색이 많고 일반 택시보다 요금이 조금 비싼 서비스 좋은 택시예요. 일반 택시는 '일반택시'라고 구분해서 말할 때가 있어요. 바로 길에서 잡거나 앱으로 부를 수 있어요.
explain_en: These are often black taxis that cost a bit more than regular ones and are known for better service. When people need to tell the two apart, they call the regular kind '일반택시'. You can hail one on the street or call one with an app.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 설명은 앞뒤가 안 맞고 모순적이에요.
examples.en: His explanation doesn't add up and is contradictory.

examples.ko: 모순적인 감정이 동시에 들 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel contradictory emotions at the same time.

examples.ko: 비싼 옷을 사면서 절약한다고 하는 건 모순적이에요.
examples.en: Buying expensive clothes while saying you're saving money is contradictory.

examples.ko: 모순적으로 들리겠지만 저는 혼자 있으면 외로우면서 편해요.
examples.en: It may sound contradictory, but when I'm alone I feel both lonely and comfortable.
Everyone was surprised by his contradictory behavior.

examples.ko: 말과 행동이 다른 건 모순적인 태도예요.
examples.en: Saying one thing and doing another is a contradictory attitude.

explain: 말, 행동, 감정이 서로 앞뒤가 안 맞을 때 써요. '모순적인 N', '모순적으로 V', '모순적이다' 모두 가능해요. 일상에서는 '앞뒤가 안 맞아요'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when words, actions or feelings don't fit together. It works as '모순적인 N', '모순적으로 V' and '모순적이다'. In daily talk, people also often say '앞뒤가 안 맞아요' (it doesn't add up).

examples.en: I dressed up a bit because I have a blind date today.
You look great even without dressing up.
My sibling spends a long time getting fancy every time they go out.
I came out in new shoes to look sharp.
Why did you get so dolled up?
I arranged the kimchi nicely and put it on a plate.

explain: 옷이나 머리를 신경 써서 멋 부리는 것이에요. '꾸미다', '멋 내다'와 가깝지만, 친한 사이에서 '좀 티 나게 차렸네' 하는 가벼운 느낌으로 자주 써요. 음식이나 물건의 겉모양을 예쁘게 만들 때도 써요.
explain_en: It means putting effort into your clothes or hair to look nice. It is close to '꾸미다' and '멋 내다', and between friends it often carries a light 'you clearly dressed up' feel. You can also use it for making food or objects look nice.

examples.en: I felt humiliated because I was scolded in front of people.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 모욕감 때문에 화가 났어요.
examples.en: After hearing that, I got angry because I felt insulted.

examples.ko: 모욕감이 들어서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I felt so insulted that I couldn't say anything.
Please don't say things that make people feel insulted.

examples.ko: 저는 그때의 모욕감을 아직도 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I still can't forget the humiliation I felt then.
My face turned red from the humiliation.

explain: '모욕감을 느끼다', '모욕감이 들다', '모욕감을 주다'로 자주 써요. 부끄러운 마음인 '수치심'과 달리, 남이 나를 무시하거나 깎아내려서 생기는 기분이에요.
explain_en: It is often used as '모욕감을 느끼다' (feel insulted), '모욕감이 들다' and '모욕감을 주다' (make someone feel insulted). Unlike '수치심' (shame), it is the feeling that comes when someone looks down on you or belittles you.

examples.en: That person kept saying insulting things.
Comparing people's looks is really insulting.
I was upset after seeing the insulting comments.
That question sounded insulting to me.
I quit the company because I was treated insultingly.

examples.ko: 손님에게 그런 모욕적인 태도를 보이면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not show that kind of insulting attitude to customers.

explain: '모욕적인 말', '모욕적으로 들리다', '모욕적이다'로 써요. '기분 나쁘다', '무례하다'보다 강하고, 상대의 자존심을 건드린다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used as '모욕적인 말' (insulting words), '모욕적으로 들리다' (sound insulting) and '모욕적이다'. It is stronger than '기분 나쁘다' (unpleasant) or '무례하다' (rude), and implies hurting someone's pride.

examples.en: The new business was an adventurous challenge.
I like adventurous trips.

examples.ko: 모험적인 성격이라 새로운 일에 겁이 없어요.
examples.en: She has an adventurous personality, so she isn't afraid of new things.
This investment is too risky.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 모험적으로 새 스타일을 시도했어요.
examples.en: That director boldly tried a new style.
I made a risky choice, but I don't regret it.

explain: 위험이 있지만 새로운 것에 도전한다는 뜻으로 사람의 성격, 선택, 시도에 써요. 좋게 말하면 '도전적', 걱정스럽게 말하면 '위험한' 느낌이 있어서 문맥에 따라 달라져요.
explain_en: It describes a person's personality, a choice or an attempt that takes risks to try something new. It can sound positive, like 'daring', or worrying, like 'risky', depending on the context.

examples.en: After exercising, my thirst is intense.

examples.ko: 시원한 물 한 잔으로 목마름을 달랬어요.
examples.en: I quenched my thirst with a glass of cold water.
I held back my thirst and walked to the end.
In the desert, thirst is the biggest problem.
When I eat salty food, I feel thirsty.

examples.ko: 오랜 목마름 끝에 마신 물이 정말 달았어요.
examples.en: After a long thirst, the water I drank tasted really sweet.

explain: '목마르다'의 명사형이에요. 일상에서는 '목말라요', '목이 말라요'가 훨씬 자연스럽고, '목마름'은 글이나 노래, 이야기에 더 자주 나와요. 비슷한 한자어는 '갈증'인데 조금 더 딱딱해요.
explain_en: This is the noun form of '목마르다'. In daily speech, '목말라요' or '목이 말라요' sounds far more natural, and '목마름' shows up more in writing, songs and stories. The Sino-Korean word '갈증' is similar but sounds a bit stiffer.

examples.ko: 졸업식에서 선생님은 목메어 말을 잇지 못하셨어요.
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony, the teacher was choked up and couldn't continue speaking.
The mother choked up as she called her son's name.
I was so happy that I greeted them in a voice choked with emotion.

examples.ko: 편지를 읽다가 목메서 더 못 읽었어요.
examples.en: I choked up while reading the letter and couldn't read on.

examples.ko: 이별 인사를 하다가 목메고 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: While saying goodbye, I choked up and started to cry.
He said thank you in a choked voice.

explain: 슬픔이나 감동 때문에 목이 막혀서 말이 잘 안 나올 때 써요. 보통은 '목이 메다'라고 띄어서 말하는 경우가 많아요. 음식이 목에 걸린 상황에는 '목에 걸리다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when sadness or deep emotion tightens your throat and words won't come out. People often say it as two words, '목이 메다'. For food stuck in the throat, use '목에 걸리다' instead.

examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I get around on crutches.
Stairs are hard because of the crutches.
I'm happy that I can walk without crutches now.
My friend came to school on crutches.
I learned how to use crutches at the hospital.

examples.ko: 목발을 짚은 사람에게 문을 잡아 줬어요.
examples.en: I held the door for a person on crutches.

explain: 다리가 아파서 걸을 때 겨드랑이에 끼고 짚는 지팡이예요. '목발을 짚다', '목발을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 손으로 잡는 '지팡이'와는 다르게 몸을 받쳐 주는 도구로 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: These are the sticks you tuck under your arms and lean on when walking with an injured leg. You say '목발을 짚다' or '목발을 쓰다'. Unlike a '지팡이' (cane) held in the hand, think of them as a tool that supports your body weight.

examples.en: I feel hurt because no one understands how I feel.
Why don't you recognize my efforts?

examples.ko: 그녀는 남자가 자기 마음을 몰라주는 게 못내 섭섭했어요.
examples.en: She felt sad that the man didn't understand her feelings.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 사정을 몰라줄 때 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was upset when my friend didn't understand my situation.
I hoped he would recognize it, but he never did.

examples.ko: 엄마는 내 고생을 몰라주는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems my mom doesn't appreciate how hard I've worked.

explain: '알아주다'의 반대로, 내 마음이나 노력, 사정을 상대가 이해하거나 인정해 주지 않을 때 써요. 단순히 모르는 게 아니라 '알아줬으면 하는데 안 알아준다'는 서운한 느낌이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '알아주다', used when someone doesn't understand or acknowledge your feelings, effort or situation. It isn't just not knowing; it carries a hurt feeling of 'I wish you had recognized this, but you didn't'.

examples.en: During vacation, I hang out with my friends in a group.
On the field trip day, the classes ran around in big groups on the playground.
As soon as exams end, students roam downtown in groups.
Shop owners don't like it when kids move around in a pack.
Don't just run around in groups every weekend; study too.
It's a street where tourists move around in crowds, so it's chaotic.

explain: 여러 사람이 무리를 지어 함께 돌아다닐 때 써요. 시끌벅적하고 조금 부정적인 느낌이 들 때가 많아요. 혼자서도 쓸 수 있는 '돌아다니다'와 달리 여럿이 함께일 때만 써요.
explain_en: Use it when many people move around together in a group. It often feels noisy and a little negative. Unlike '돌아다니다', which you can do alone, this only works when several people are together.

examples.en: That player moves lightly and quickly.

examples.ko: 나이가 드니 몸놀림이 예전 같지 않아요.
examples.en: As I get older, my movements aren't what they used to be.
The dance teacher's movements are really smooth.
I was startled by the cat's quick movements.
There is strength in every single movement.

examples.ko: 그는 느린 몸놀림으로 공을 겨우 잡았어요.
examples.en: He barely caught the ball with his slow movements.

explain: 몸을 움직이는 모습이나 솜씨를 말해요. '가볍다', '빠르다', '둔하다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 뜻을 전하려는 동작인 '몸짓'과 달리, 움직임 자체가 어떤지를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to how the body moves or how skillfully it moves. It often appears with '가볍다' (light), '빠르다' (fast) and '둔하다' (clumsy). Unlike '몸짓', which is a gesture meant to communicate, it describes the quality of the movement itself.

examples.en: I had an appointment, so I started getting ready from the morning.
It takes a whole hour to get myself ready.
Please groom yourself neatly before the interview.
After I finished getting ready, I looked in the mirror once.

examples.ko: 할머니는 외출 전에 꼭 몸단장을 하세요.
examples.en: My grandmother always grooms herself before going out.
Before welcoming guests, I got myself ready first.

explain: 옷, 머리, 화장 등을 단정하게 갖추는 것이에요. '몸단장을 하다'로 많이 말하고, 멋을 부리는 '모양내다'보다 깔끔하게 갖춘다는 느낌이 더 커요.
explain_en: It means putting yourself in order with clothes, hair and makeup. It is mostly used as '몸단장을 하다', and it feels more like making yourself neat and presentable than the showy dressing up of '모양내다'.

examples.ko: 저는 십 년 동안 이 회사에 몸담았어요.
examples.en: I worked at this company for ten years.

examples.ko: 교육 분야에 몸담고 있는 분을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met someone who works in the field of education.

examples.ko: 옛날 자신이 몸담았던 부대를 보자 반가웠어요.
examples.en: He felt glad when he saw the unit he used to belong to.
Which club are you a member of?

examples.ko: 몸담은 지 오래된 곳이라 정이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I've been part of this place for a long time, so I've grown attached to it.

examples.ko: 그 일에 몸담으면서 많은 걸 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned a lot while working in that field.

explain: '회사에 몸담다', '이 분야에 몸담다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 단순히 '일하다'보다 그 조직이나 분야에 속해 오래 있었다는 느낌이 있고, 조금 격식 있게 들려요.
explain_en: It is used with '에', as in '회사에 몸담다' or '이 분야에 몸담다'. Compared with plain '일하다', it suggests belonging to that organization or field for a while, and it sounds a bit formal.

examples.en: I felt achy since morning, so I rested early.
When I feel achy, I drink warm water.
I overdid it yesterday, so I'm starting to feel achy.
I feel chilly because I'm coming down with something.

examples.ko: 약을 먹고 자니 몸살기가 좀 가라앉았어요.
examples.en: After taking medicine and sleeping, the achiness calmed down a bit.
I'm achy, but I don't have a fever.

explain: 몸살이 나기 전에 온몸이 쑤시고 으슬으슬한 약한 기운이에요. '몸살기가 있다', '몸살기가 돌다'처럼 말해요. 완전히 아픈 '몸살이 나다'보다 가벼운 단계예요.
explain_en: This is the weak, early sign of being sick, when your whole body aches and you feel chilly. You say '몸살기가 있다' or '몸살기가 돌다'. It is a milder stage than fully getting sick, as in '몸살이 나다'.

examples.ko: 그때 일을 생각하면 아직도 몸서리가 나요.
examples.en: When I think about that time, I still shudder.
I shudder whenever I see a bug.
I shuddered after hearing a ghost story.
That movie was so scary that it made me shudder.

examples.ko: 고생했던 기억에 몸서리가 나서 다시는 안 가요.
examples.en: The memory of hardship makes me shudder, so I'll never go again.
I shudder whenever exams come up.

explain: 무섭거나 싫을 때 몸이 부르르 떨리는 것이에요. '몸서리가 나다', '몸서리를 치다'로 자주 써요. 싫은 기억이나 무서운 일 앞에서 쓰고, 추워서 떠는 것은 보통 '떨다'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the sudden trembling of the body when something is frightening or unpleasant. It is commonly used as '몸서리가 나다' or '몸서리를 치다'. Use it for bad memories or scary things; for shaking from cold, people usually say '떨다'.

examples.ko: 아기를 낳고 한 달 동안 몸조리를 했어요.
examples.en: After giving birth, I rested and recovered for a month.

examples.ko: 감기 심하게 걸렸다면서요? 푹 쉬고 몸조리 잘하세요.
examples.en: I heard you caught a bad cold. Rest well and take care of yourself.
After surgery, you have to rest and recover at home.
My mom came to help me with my recovery.
If you don't take care of yourself during recovery, you'll suffer later.
After leaving the hospital, I recovered at my country house.

explain: 아프거나 아기를 낳은 뒤에 쉬면서 건강을 되찾는 것이에요. 아픈 사람에게 '몸조리 잘하세요'라고 하면 '푹 쉬고 잘 회복하세요'라는 인사말이 돼요. 출산 후에는 '산후조리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means resting and regaining your health after an illness or childbirth. Telling a sick person '몸조리 잘하세요' works as a greeting meaning 'rest well and recover'. After childbirth it is also called '산후조리'.

examples.en: Let's talk about what we couldn't finish saying tomorrow.
Please pack the food I couldn't finish eating.

examples.ko: 오늘 못다 읽은 책은 주말에 읽을 거예요.
examples.en: I'll read the book I couldn't finish today over the weekend.

examples.ko: 친구에게 못다 한 말이 아직 많아요.
examples.en: There is still a lot I haven't been able to say to my friend.
I couldn't finish my homework, so I told the teacher.

examples.ko: 시간이 없어서 못다 쓴 일기를 이어서 썼어요.
examples.en: I didn't have time earlier, so I continued writing the diary I hadn't finished.

explain: '끝까지 다 하지 못한'이라는 느낌으로 동사 앞에 붙여 '못다 한 말', '못다 읽은 책'처럼 써요. '다 못 했다'와 비슷하지만 '못다 한 ~'은 아쉬움이 남은 느낌이라 노래나 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Put it before a verb to give the sense of 'couldn't finish all the way', as in '못다 한 말' (words left unsaid) or '못다 읽은 책' (a book not finished). It is similar to '다 못 했다', but '못다 한 ~' leaves a feeling of regret, so it often appears in songs and writing.
